Nonvertex fundamental disk reduces to connected disk+disk or sphere+annulus summands resolving to two disk copies. This reduction is not a contradiction.

discarded_shortcut.actual_obstruction: Cap replacement also adds/removes whole normal face arcs inside the cap, without exchange endpoints. Their contributions can balance the exchange-arc incidence. Equal whole-disk vectors do not alone force that incidence to vanish. No theorem or source proof was authored using the shortcut.

single_copy_inverse_research.setting: Undo one exchange of an actual original-diagram full resolution, with both traces on one fundamental disk component; all other exchanges remain regular.
single_copy_inverse_research.proved_from_existing_interfaces: If that normalization disconnects the disk into two pieces, each is embedded normal (the one remaining double curve must join the components), producing a nontrivial coordinate decomposition, impossible by fundamentalness.
single_copy_inverse_research.four_ray_classification: At frontier points p,q, label upper rays0,1 and lower rays2,3. The actual crossing inverse pairs0–3 and1–2. Thus proper-disk nonadjacent outer caps split off a disk and annulus/Mobius piece; disjoint-annulus nonadjacent caps split off a sphere and punctured genus piece. Nested annulus caps split only in the adjacent nested configuration.
single_copy_inverse_research.scope_limit: The other nested annulus configuration can retain one immersed normalization. Fundamentalness alone does not close it. A weight-replacement argument needs the exact annular patch positivity/cancellation proof, which is not inferred from disk-patch positivity.
single_copy_inverse_research.source_note: Suh Lemmas3.7–3.11 and Theorem3.12 actual full text reread. Its preliminary nested-cap reduction and global support-extension matching still need explicit local proofs for this project; no citation used as a supplier.
